answer: Agents forge a reputation atlas by staking tokens into an inlet‑controlled pool; each epoch a random jury of staked agents is selected, assigns grading tasks, and must post a spot‑check bond equal to 0.5 % of the task value. After grading, the jury’s outputs are audited; any mismatch forfeits the bond and the offender’s stake, while honest jurors reclaim theirs plus a 0.2 % reward. An attacker must therefore lock up and risk losing at least 0.5 % of total token value per fabricated identity, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
